I read them as payouts to a surviving relative.\n- **Who the claimants point to:** Each of those three is the emergency contact of exactly four patients.\n- **Who is still alive:** In each group, the other patients filed ordinary claims 3–16 days after the payout, so they were alive then. Nine of the ten dependents who filed did this. A pattern that tight is very unlikely by chance (roughly 5 in 10 million under a random-timing baseline).\n- **Who is left:** One patient per group has no claim after the payout.\n  - **PAT_174** (Rowan Rivera) never filed a claim. Their contact is PAT_033.\n  - **PAT_023** (Morgan Lane) never filed a claim. Their contact is PAT_265.\n  - **PAT_102** (Skyler Jones) last filed on 2025-06-08, 30 days before PAT_006's payout, and nothing since. Their contact is PAT_006.\n\n**Weaknesses**\n- Two of the three, PAT_174 and PAT_023, are \"no claim\" patients, and about half the registry never filed a claim, so silence alone proves little. They are picked because their contact collected a death-style payout.\n- PAT_102 is the weakest pick. They filed once before the payout and nothing after, and unlike the other two they have a record. They are also the only dependent in their group who filed before the payout, which fits the pattern but is thin evidence.\n- I didn't find any independent confirmation of death, such as a mutual contact or a payment tied to a date for any of the three.","ttft_ms":3222,"type":"result","duration_ms":3072715,"uuid":"58307f7a-079d-4a5f-8703-9bbe385a34f3","ttft_stream_ms":3221,"time_to_request_ms":81,"first_content_frame_ms":3221,"queued_turn_count":0,"result_index":0}
